column2: applying `ci_wait_initial_empty_checks_grace_sec` via `empty_checks_grace` while leaving `ci_monitor` unchanged reuses single blocking sleep semantics. on the first empty rollup, `gather_status` sleeps the full grace once, then re-queries once. a new pr whose first `gh pr checks` response is empty (common) therefore waits the full ~300s before learning checks started, instead of detecting them on 10s polls. that is a happy-path latency regression relative to `grace=0`, distinct from the runless-head hang the issue targets.

the `no_checks` terminal `last_monitored_head` guard is not tied to the helper rename. the bail path persists `last_monitored_head` only when `post_push_grace > 0`. the plan renames that binding to `empty_checks_grace` but does not explicitly require updating this guard to the same variable/expression used for `monitor()`. a partial rename causes `nameerror`, or narrowing the condition to post-fix-only grace breaks #4867 resume seeding after post-push `no_checks` stalls.

python/ship.py:1541-1563, python/ship.py:1720-1725 [scope-reduction] all-zero counters can keep the 300s initial grace active after monitor progress. scenario: ci_monitor.monitor can return ok for evaluate_failure with ci-still-in-progress without incrementing iteration, rebase_count, fix_attempts, or transient_retries; the next loop still has all counters zero, so the proposed helper would pass the 300s initial grace again instead of limiting it to the first ci wait

a startup-deadline "is the rollup still empty?" probe must not rely on `checks_status(..., empty_checks_grace=0)` or on classified `pending` alone. `_resolve_checks_status` maps both a zero-row rollup and a rollup with in-flight pending jobs to `status=="pending"` when `grace=0` (empty bucket returns `("pending", none)` at line 422; `_classify_checks_json` pending rows do the same). startup-deadline accounting keyed off that signal can treat actively running ci as still-empty, never clear the timer, and bail `no_checks` at ~300s while checks are running; slow-start prs can also be misread as empty and false-bail.

python/ci_monitor.py:554-626 startup-deadline no_checks bail needs explicit poll_ci control-flow placement and return shape. scenario: plan adds deadline accounting but does not pin where it runs inside the existing loop. if implemented before decide(), a behind/rebase/merge path can be skipped; if after sleep/increment, empty time is under-counted or a rebase/merge decision is missed; if only decision is set while cistatus stays pending, poll_ci tests and the grace>0 no_checks contract diverge

python/test_ship.py:116-132 plan extends last_monitored_head terminal guard tests only for post-push empty_checks_grace>0, not for initial startup-deadline-only no_checks. scenario: the renamed bounded_empty_checks guard (empty_checks_grace>0 or empty_checks_startup_deadline_sec>0) is untested on the initial-wait path; an implementer can wire monitor() kwargs correctly but still persist terminal_last_head=none when grace=0 and only the startup deadline fired, regressing #4867 resume seeding for that bail shape
